hints.title: Triangular Sum Bound Obstacle
hints.text: Building k complete staircase rows requires k * (k + 1) // 2 total coins. What is the maximum complete row count k such that required coins do not exceed n?

hints.title: Triangular Monotonic Invariant
hints.text: The coin requirement f(k) = k * (k + 1) // 2 strictly increases with k. If f(mid) <= n, mid rows are feasible, so search for larger k; otherwise search smaller.

hints.title: Row Bisection Procedure
hints.text: Initialize left = 0, right = n. While left <= right, let mid = (left + right) // 2. Compute coins = mid * (mid + 1) // 2. If coins <= n, save ans = mid and try left = mid + 1; otherwise right = mid - 1. Return ans.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

complexity.notes: Logarithmic bisection over staircase row heights in O(1) space.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Subtracting row heights iteratively takes O(sqrt(N)) operations, running up to 65,536 iterations.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Using 64-bit integers to prevent overflow when computing mid * (mid + 1) for large n.
